findings.issue: Since the D-2 deviation, the createAdviceWorker option is used only if no app-wide client exists yet. main.tsx creates it in production, and both harnesses call sharedAdviceClient(createAdviceWorker) before mounting and then pass the same factory as a prop. So the prop never chooses anything, and a caller passing a different factory later is silently ignored. It is also in the effect deps for no reason.
findings.evidence: e2e/support/table-harness.tsx:11 and :20, e2e/support/advice-harness.tsx:45 and :52 both prime the shared client and also pass the prop; advice-client.ts sharedAdviceClient uses `shared ??=`.
findings.fix: Keep the seam as the fix brief asks, but make its doc comment say it is ignored once the app-wide client exists, and drop the redundant prop from the two harness <Table> calls (or drop the option entirely in a later story). If you keep it, remove it from the effect deps.

findings.issue: sharedAdviceClient(createAdviceWorker) runs inside the setTimeout callback outside the promise chain. If no client exists yet and the factory throws synchronously (for example Worker is unavailable or blocked by CSP), the error escapes as an uncaught timer error instead of going through the setTable rethrow (D-7). The table then waits on a bot turn forever. This can't happen in production today, because main.tsx creates the client first and a throw there crashes the load visibly.
findings.evidence: The rejection handler covers only decideBot's promise; the client lookup before it is unguarded.
findings.fix: Start the chain with Promise.resolve().then(() => sharedAdviceClient(createAdviceWorker).decideBot(turn.view, turn.style)) so a creation failure takes the same reject -> setTable(throw) path.

findings.issue: After an error or messageerror the client is permanently failed, but the worker is not terminated and stays alive for the rest of the app session. With the shared worker this means one leaked thread per page load at most.
findings.evidence: #onFailure calls #fail, which removes the listeners but never calls terminate(); only dispose() terminates.
findings.fix: Call this.#worker.terminate() in #onFailure after #fail (SPEC-09 still holds: dispose terminates once, because #disposed guards it).

findings.issue: With the shared worker, leaving a table mid-computation only drops the reply (cancelled flag). The worker still finishes that computation, so the next table's first bot request queues behind it. This is harmless at real speed. It is the accepted cost of Option A, and the 'Not doing' list excludes cancelling in-flight work.
findings.evidence: Spec §7 'Interruption' assumed dispose on unmount; that behaviour was replaced by the D-2 deviation.
findings.fix: None needed now. Note it in the story doc next to the D-2 deviation.

summary: Implementation matches the spec, and the recorded D-2 deviation holds up on substance. Stale replies: the cancelled flag (any table change re-runs the effect) plus the applyBotDecision hand-identity check mean a reply can never apply to another hand or after unmount. StrictMode clears the timer before any post, so there are no duplicate requests. Errors: service throws become ok:false; worker error/messageerror reject all pending and later calls, and the hook rethrows inside setTable as D-7 requires, so there is no hang for a crashing worker. The one gap is a synchronous factory throw in the timer, which production avoids (MINOR). Only {id, kind, view, style} is posted, as asserted in SPEC-06 with a fast-check permutation of the hidden cards; no replay code or hidden cards cross. Worker results equal headless play in Node over MessageChannel (SPEC-05, 50 hands) and in the browser (SPEC-04). SSR safety: the advice-client module only declares a null singleton; the Worker is built only in main.tsx (never imported by tests) or in effects/timers. SPEC-10 verified: the dist build has no tlh-test-slow-advice marker and exactly one advice.worker chunk. The SPEC-15 guard would fail if decisions moved back to the main thread: windows would be empty and toHaveLength(bots.length) would fail. Timing tests are gated by TLH_SLOW_TESTS and engine skips. Ran the new spec: 4 passed, 6 skipped. The three new Vitest files pass. Locked tests are unchanged per git diff. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
